about: What tools/types.mjs builds each type's page from (examples/types/<type>.json and .html): for each type (the map and docs/types.md's 28), its page's title and its variants, in card order. A variant source is an example of examples/ ("sales-classes" is examples/sales-classes.json) or a variant file ("variants/uml-class-down" is examples/variants/uml-class-down.json, named <type>-<name>); each of its views of the type gets a card on the page's overview: its sub (a short line on the card) and its text (what the view shows, in the card's details). Plain keyboard characters; `code` in backticks.

shapes.text: A card of each kind that has a shape, in the one style maps draw: people, a browser app, a phone, a window (a card's own `shape`), a terminal, an agent, a database, a queue, a file, a module, hosts, a hook and an external system.

boxed.text: A map generated from a dependency list by `monorepo.py`: a card per package, a line per import, its weight (more imports) showing on hover, selection and focus and in its tooltip, a box per folder, nested as the folders are.

plain.text: The same packages and imports as the boxed view, with no boxes: the layout without folders.

lines.text: A library's holds as lines of each kind, drawn in its colour: calls, feeds, triggers, state and guard; weights 1 to 3, each shown as a width on hover, selection and focus and in the line's tooltip; numbered steps, 4a and 4b among them; and a line's sublabel under its label.

boxes.text: A cafe chain's systems in boxes: two nested in a head office box, a tinted box with a tone, badges on a box's border, cards with owners, and two lenses, one ringing cards by owner and one lighting the lines that feed data.

badges.text: A bakery's order cards with icons, badges as plain tabs and in tones, an edit mark on a card and on a line, and a card with `noSub`, its description kept for the details panel.

domain.text: Compartments of attributes and operations, an interface, an enumeration and a data type, composition and aggregation, generalization, realization, a `<<use>>` dependency and a note, each end with its role and multiplicity.

payments-only.text: Four classes of the sales domain named plainly from the view's `subject`, Order with its compartments collapsed, laid out down.

members.text: Every member notation: the four visibilities (+ - # ~), a static attribute and operation underlined, a derived attribute, defaults and multiplicities, parameters with their direction, an abstract class and operation in italics, a primitive type and a data type, and a class cut to 3 rows then "+k more".

lines.text: Every kind of line a class view draws: an association navigable both ways, roles and multiplicities, composite and shared aggregation, an interface realization, a usage, an abstraction, a plain dependency with a name and a comment link, listed in the view's `edges`.

right.text: An abstract class with four specializations and two interfaces, laid out right (the default direction): generalizations and realizations as hollow triangles, an enumeration used by an interface.

down.text: The same hierarchy with `direction: "down"`: the general class above its specializations, the interfaces beside it and each class's place pinned in `layout`.

snapshot.text: Instances of the bookshop's classes, each head `name : Classifier` underlined, slots as `feature = value`, and links with a name or roles by their ends.

branch.sub: a package box, stereotypes, a note
branch.text: Library loan instances held in a package drawn as a box, two of them with an <<entity>> stereotype, an anonymous instance shown as `: Copy`, an instance with no classifier, a slot with no value, a link named by its association, and a note on the anonymous copy.

unboxed.text: The same instances without their package, so each is named `lending::loan7 : Loan`, laid out down.

beside.text: Cycle hire docks and a bike drawn beside the Dock and Bike classes their slots are checked against, two links between one pair each on its own line, and a link from an instance to itself drawn as a loop.

packages.text: Packages as boxes holding what they own, a package inside a package, two classes named Order in two packages, `<<import>>`, `<<access>>`, `<<merge>>` and a dependency between them, and a profile applied by `<<apply>>`.

closed.text: Five packages with none of their contents in the view, so each is drawn as a closed folder with its name in the body; `<<subsystem>>` and `<<library>>` stereotypes, a public import, a private import drawn as `<<access>>`, a `<<use>>` dependency and a note on one package.

nested.sub: three levels deep, laid out down
nested.text: A package inside a package inside a package, each box holding its classes, an enumeration and an interface; an import from lending to catalogue, and `<<use>>` and `<<call>>` dependencies that cross the box borders.

qualified.text: The same classes with no package drawn: the view's `subject` is the library package, so each class is named by the packages between it and the subject, such as lending::holds::Hold.

internals.text: A class's parts and ports, a part showing its type's ports, connectors through parts, open collaborations and collaboration uses with their role bindings.

inside.text: A component as the subject: parts with multiplicities such as `1..*` and `0..1`, a shared part drawn dashed, ports on the component and on its parts' types, connectors through them, the component's two ports pinned to opposite sides in `present`, and a comment linked to a port.

roles.text: A collaboration as the view's subject: its roles drawn as parts with their types and multiplicities, and the connectors that join the roles.

components.text: Components nested in components, ports on their borders, delegations inward, assembly connectors, provided and required interfaces as a ball and socket, artifacts and their manifestations.

packages.text: Library components in packages, two classes realizing a component (dashed, hollow triangle), an interface drawn as a box with its operations, provided and required by dashed lines, a `<<call>>` dependency and a plain one, an artifact's `<<manifest>>` and a note.

sockets.text: A cinema's booking laid out down: interfaces as balls with their sockets, typed ports (`seats : SeatPicker`) joined by an assembly, delegations into and out of a component's parts, and two parts joined directly.

production.text: Nodes, devices and execution environments as cubes, nested; artifacts deployed by nesting or by a `<<deploy>>` line; deployment specifications and communication paths.

docks.text: A bike dock network laid out down: a node inside a node inside a data centre, execution environments on devices, a stereotyped device, a deployment specification and paths that end on a box's border.

lines.text: A library catalogue whose artifacts stand apart from their targets: each deployed by a dashed `<<deploy>>` line, a deployment specification deployed the same way, `<<manifest>>` lines to components and stereotyped server nodes.

profile.text: Stereotypes with tag definitions extending metaclasses, a required extension, a profile applied to a package, and an element's tags in a compartment per stereotype; stereotypes applied anywhere in the model are checked against it.

fleet-profile.text: A cycle hire profile whose abstract <<asset>> stereotype is specialized by <<vehicle>> and <<station>>, a tag typed by the profile's own enumeration, a tag with a default, and classes showing their tags in a compartment per stereotype, inherited tags included.

two-profiles.text: A library package applying two profiles that both define <<record>>, told apart as `Storage::record` and `Audit::record`, and a required extension of Package that puts <<owner>> over a closed package with no stereotype stored.

shopping.text: Actors as stick figures, use cases as ellipses with their extension points, the subject as a box holding them, and include, extend and generalization between them.

dock.text: Two subjects side by side, the dock kiosk and the rider app, each holding its own use cases, laid out down; a `<<system>>` actor, an include, an extend at the extension point "after locking" with its condition, and a note on a use case.

lending.text: Use cases with no subject box around them; actors specialized two levels deep (a junior member is a member is a borrower), two use cases specializing one, and an include.

fulfil.text: Actions, object nodes and a data store, send and accept actions, decisions, merges, forks and joins, in lanes; a call behaviour action opens the activity it calls.

take-payment.text: The activity the call behaviour action Take payment calls: its own actions and flows, opened from the fulfilling activity.

return-right.sub: a loop, laid out right, no lanes
return-right.text: An activity with no lanes laid out right: a retry loop through a named merge, two decisions with `[yes]` and `[else]` guards, a send signal action, a flow final and an activity final, and a comment on a decision.

rebalance.text: Partitions nested in a partition (Operations holds the control room and the van crew), laid out right: a data store and an object node on object flows, then a send signal action that an accept event action in another lane takes up.

order-life.text: States with their activities, composite states as boxes with orthogonal regions, a choice, a fork and a join, a shallow history and a terminate, and transitions written `trigger [guard] / effect`.

loan.sub: deep history, a junction, a note
loan.text: A library loan: a composite state left on a closure and re-entered by its deep history (H*), a junction merging two returns, an internal transition with a guard, a final state and a note on the history.

machine.text: A coffee machine laid out down: entry, do and exit rows, two internal transitions, Brewing as a closed composite with UML's decomposition mark (its substates not shown), and Descaling with its activities collapsed.

checkout-sequence.text: Lifelines on a time axis, calls, a self-call, async messages, replies and a create, activation bars derived from the messages, `alt` and `opt` frames with their guards, and an interaction use.

find-book.text: The sequence view the interaction overview's use Find a book opens: a short exchange between lifelines.

buy-checkout.text: The sequence view the interaction overview's use Check out opens.

email-receipt.text: The sequence view the interaction overview's use Email the receipt opens.

queue-order.text: The sequence view the interaction overview's inline interaction Queue the order shows.

unlock.text: Unlocking a hire bike: a `break` frame when the rider has no credit, a `loop` frame for the ride, a trip lifeline created and later deleted with a cross, and async messages stereotyped `<<mqtt>>`.

parallel.text: Returning a library book: a `par` frame whose two operands run at once, an `opt` frame nested in one of them, a self-call and replies to each call.

checkout-communication.text: The checkout's paid branch as lifelines joined by connectors, each link's messages a stack of numbered rows with an arrow toward the receiver.

unlock.text: Unlocking a hire bike laid out down: numbers nested to four levels (1.1.2.1), a message with a <<secure>> stereotype after its number, a token created and then deleted, and a connector to the station map that carries no message.

hold-ready.text: A returned library book freeing a hold: two asynchronous messages with open arrows, a guard written as text in front of a call, and replies that return along the connector their call came by.

buy-book.text: Interaction uses and an inline interaction drawn with its sequence diagram inside, joined by the activity's control nodes and flows; each use, and the inline interaction, opens its sequence view.

rent.sub: laid out right, flow final, a note
rent.text: Four interaction uses laid out right, each opening its own sequence view; named flows, a decision with guards, a flow final node that ends one branch only, and a note on it.

return-book.text: Two inline interactions drawn as sd frames with their sequence diagrams inside, and an interaction use between them on one branch of a decision, joined again by a merge node, laid out down.

one-charge.text: Lifelines on one linear time ruler, each a step line through its states or a band of values, messages at their times, duration and time constraints.

unlock.text: Two state lifelines and one drawn as a band of values (`present.<lifeline>.as: "values"`), in seconds: asynchronous messages, one with a `<<signal>>` stereotype, a duration constraint between two lifelines and a time constraint.

charging.text: A longer run in minutes: a call and its reply, an asynchronous message, a battery's value band, and overlapping duration constraints on one lifeline drawn on their own levels.

order-flows.text: Information items, and dashed `<<flow>>` lines between classifiers and actors, each saying what it conveys.

classes.text: Flows between an actor, classes and an interface, each named (`<<flow>> borrow: Card number, Copy`), one conveying a class beside information items, a flow from a class to itself and a note.

orders.text: A cafe's orders laid out down: a guest, a barista and three components, an order, a ticket and the beans used flowing between them.

requirements.text: Requirements with their id and text in a frame with SysML's header; containment drawn with a crosshair; derive, satisfy, verify, refine, trace and copy, each checked as SysML says.

kinds.text: A dock station's requirements in a package the frame names as its subject: the five requirement kinds over their names, each with its risk and verify method rows, and a `<<problem>>` note.

trace.text: Library self-checkout: requirements derived from one whose long text is cut to 3 rows then "+n more", blocks that satisfy them, test cases that verify them and a block that refines one.

blocks.text: Blocks, interface blocks, constraint blocks and value types with SysML's named compartments; composition, generalization and dependency.

charging.text: A cycle hire charging dock framed by its package (`bdd [Package] Charging`): proxy ports typed by an interface block and by its conjugate (`~ChargeLink`), a full port typed by a block, flow properties in, out and inout, and an interface block's operation.

fleet.text: Fleet vehicles specializing one block, value properties with defaults and multiplicities typed by value types with units and quantity kinds, a value type specializing another, a part drawn as a composite line, and a reference drawn as a plain association.

inside-ebike.text: A block's parts, references and values inside its frame; proxy and full ports with flow arrows and conjugation; connectors with item flows.

inside-station.sub: frame ports, delegation, a full port
inside-station.text: A dock station's parts, a reference and a value; a proxy port on the frame delegating to the charger's port, a full port on the frame, conjugated proxy ports meeting, and item flows on four connectors.

inside-charger.sub: a part's own block, two delegations
inside-charger.text: The charger, a part of the dock, as the subject of its own diagram: its two frame ports delegate in to the breaker and out from the rectifier, with alternating current flowing between them.

range-analysis.text: Constraint properties with their expressions, parameters on their borders, binding connectors to the block's value properties.

frame.sub: a constraint block as the frame
frame.text: A constraint block as the subject: its own parameters on the frame, bound to the parameters of three constraint properties whose expressions add a thinking distance to a braking distance.

power-down.sub: a power budget, laid out down
power-down.text: A block's value properties bound through two chained constraint properties, a charging load and the supply headroom, with `direction: "down"`.

c4-context.text: The bookshop as a system among its people and external systems, on the map's card shapes.

c4-containers.text: The bookshop's containers inside its dashed boundary, each with its technology; implied relationships drawn where a view hides an end.

c4-components.text: The Shop API's components inside its boundary, with the containers and systems they talk to.

c4-placing-an-order.text: A dynamic view: placing an order as numbered steps between the containers.

c4-deployment.text: Deployment nodes nested as boxes, holding the container instances that run in production.

landscape.text: A landscape view: the city libraries' software systems side by side with the people who use them and two external systems, with no system as its subject.

shapes.text: A container view whose containers use C4's card shapes by `shape`: a browser, a phone, a window, a robot, a terminal, a cylinder, a pipe and a folder, beside the default box and a grey external system.

er-schema.text: Tables and their columns as rows, related in crow's foot or IDEF1X on one geometry: a composite key, a junction table, a nullable foreign key, a self-reference.

idef1x.text: A cycle hire schema in IDEF1X: identifying relationships make dock and hire_point dependent entities with rounded corners, a dot and P or Z at each child, a diamond at an optional parent.

crowsfoot-down.text: The same schema in crow's foot laid out down, showing all four end forms (exactly one, zero or one, one or more, zero or more) and a note on a table.

rows.text: A library catalogue where the title table is cut to 4 rows then "+n more" and the copy table shows its key only, its other columns collapsed; nullable and unique columns marked.

dfd-level-1.text: Level 1 in Yourdon notation: numbered processes, data stores and external entities joined by labelled data flows; a process opens its level.

dfd-level-2-take-order.text: Level 2 of process 1, Take order: its own processes and stores, checked for balance against the flows of its parent process.

rides.text: Cycle hire rides in Gane and Sarson notation: processes as rounded rectangles with their number in a top band, data stores as open rectangles with an id box, external entities with a shadow, a request and its reply between one pair, and a note.

context.text: A library's lending as one process, numbered 0, with the external entities it trades data with; the process opens its level 1.

level-1.text: Process 0 broken into 0.1 to 0.3, laid out down, with a local data store that the balance check against the context diagram leaves out.

returns.text: Ten symbols, laid out down: terminators, processes, a decision with labelled exits, input/output, a predefined process, a document, a database, manual input, a delay and a connector.

unlock.sub: laid out right, three exits, a loop
unlock.text: Laid out right: a decision with three labelled exits, one of which loops back to it through a manual input, a delay, a database, a document and two end terminators.

renew.sub: an on-page connector pair, a note
renew.text: Two connectors labelled B: the flow goes into one and carries on from the other, so the chart breaks without a long line; two decisions, a manual input and a note on the connector.

order-to-shipment.text: BPMN 2.0.2's Descriptive elements: pools and lanes, tasks, a collapsed sub-process that opens its own view, events with their markers, gateways, boundary events on an activity's border, message flows between pools, data, an annotation and a group.

pick-and-pack.text: The collapsed sub-process Pick and pack, opened as its own view: its tasks and events between its start and end.

hold.text: One pool with lanes nested in a lane, an expanded sub-process drawn as a frame round its own flow and gateways, a none intermediate throw event, a non-interrupting timer boundary event (dashed) and a message end event.

billing.sub: black-box pools, data, laid out down
billing.text: A collaboration laid out down: two black-box pools, a timer start event, a data store and a data object each read by a task, message flows to and from the pools, a message catch event, a message end event and a text annotation on a directed association.

mm-plan.text: A tree of topics laid out left and right of its root, branches as curves in the map's kind colours, edited by N, F2, Alt + arrows and drops; Mermaid mindmaps imported.

year.text: Every first-level branch set to the right by `present.side`, three levels below the root, and a long topic wrapped to four lines inside its box.

move.text: No `side` given, so each branch goes to the shorter half; the Moving day topic carries the drill-down mark and opens its own mindmap.

moving-day.text: The mindmap the Moving day topic opens, a tree of its own under the first view.

aws-on-aws.text: Accounts, regions, VPCs, availability zones, subnets and security groups as nested boxes, each service or resource a card with its icon and full service name. On this site the icons are the vendor's own, fetched with AWS's terms accepted; in a copy of this repository the diagram draws glyphs until you fetch them with `umlimator.py pack fetch aws`. Umlimator is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Amazon Web Services, Google or Microsoft.

serverless.text: A cycle hire API with no VPC: a region holding managed services, a generic group of functions that a line leaves from its border, and riders on a mobile client.

accounts.text: A library's production account and its log archive account side by side in one cloud, a VPC, a private subnet and a security group nested in turn, and a line from the VPC's border to a bucket in the other account.

gcp-on-gcp.text: Groups nested as boxes titled with their kind, each product a card with its icon and full service name, lines to a group's border. On this site the icons are the vendor's own, fetched with Google's terms accepted; in a copy of this repository the diagram draws glyphs until you fetch them with `umlimator.py pack fetch gcp`. Umlimator is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Amazon Web Services, Google or Microsoft.

telemetry.sub: a generic group, lines to groups
telemetry.text: Cycle hire dock telemetry: a generic group inside a project, a line that ends on that group's border, a line to a second project drawn as a closed card because nothing it holds is shown, and a label broken over two lines by the author.

two-regions.text: A library catalogue served from two regions of one project, laid out down: global products in the project, the same service in each region, and readers reaching DNS, the load balancer and the CDN directly.

az-on-azure.text: Subscriptions, resource groups, regions, virtual networks and subnets as nested boxes, each service a card with its icon and full service name. On this site the icons are the vendor's own, fetched with Microsoft's terms accepted; in a copy of this repository the diagram draws glyphs until you fetch them with `umlimator.py pack fetch azure`. Umlimator is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Amazon Web Services, Google or Microsoft.

regions.text: Two dashed regions in one resource group, each running the same pair of services behind a traffic manager, laid out down; a label broken over two lines, and lines that start at a region's border. Icons come from the pack you fetch, as on the first card.

landing.text: Three subscriptions whose services the view hides, each drawn as a closed card, joined by lines that end on the groups themselves, and a generic group holding two services. Icons come from the pack you fetch, as on the first card.
